record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer-part sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-fold mean convergence for a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) satisfies one of the three asymptotic alternatives stated in the paper: either |a(t) - c p(t)| / log t → ∞ for every real c and integer polynomial p, or a(t) - c p(t) → d for some real c, d, or |a(t) - t/m| ≤ C log t for some nonzero integer m and constant C?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Let F be as above. Show that the family of sequences {([a1(n)]), . . . , ([a`(n)])} is good for `-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every function a ∈ span∗(F) satisfies one of the following conditions: • |a(t) − cp(t)|/ log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]; or • a(t) − cp(t) → d for some c, d ∈ R; or • |a(t) − t/m| ≤ C log t for some non-zero m ∈ Z and C > 0.

artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along Hardy field sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Frantzikinakis–Kuca and the survey "Joint ergodicity – 40 years on") confirms several Hardy-field conjectures of Frantzikinakis and proves convergence in many cases, but the searched sources do not explicitly state that the precise three-alternative characterization for $\ell$-fold mean convergence has been fully established. The status of this exact equivalence is therefore unclear from available sources.
